title: Transformations: Translation, Reflection, Rotation and Enlargement
seo_title: Transformations – SSS 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Describe and carry out translations, reflections, rotations and enlargements on the Cartesian plane. (summary of the NERDC SSS 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 3 maths worksheets on transformations: translations, reflections in lines, rotations about the origin and enlargements with scale factors. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Reflection in y = x swaps the coordinates
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A translation moves every point by the same vector.
  • Reflection in the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y); in the y-axis: (x, y) → (−x, y).
  • Rotation 90° anticlockwise about O: (x, y) → (−y, x). Enlargement scale factor k from O: (x, y) → (kx, ky).

Examples

Example

Rotate (3, 1) by 180° about O

(x, y) → (−x, −y)

Answer: (−3, −1)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing clockwise and anticlockwise90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x).
Enlarging from the wrong centreMeasure from the centre.
Changing size in a rotationRotations keep the size.

faq.q: What does a negative scale factor do?
faq.a: It enlarges and turns the shape upside down through the centre.

items.q: Point A(5, −3) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x − 3, y + 4). What are the coordinates of A′?
Point A(3, 1) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x + 3, y − 4). What are the coordinates of A′?
Point A(5, −4) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x − 6, y + 5). What are the coordinates of A′?
A translation by the rule (x, y) → (x + 6, y + 7) maps point A to A′(1, 8). What are the coordinates of A?
items.e: Undo the translation: subtract 6 from x and 7 from y. A = (−5, 1).

Point A(1, −4) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x + 5, y + 4). What are the coordinates of A′?
A translation maps A(−1, −2) to A′(2, −1). Which rule describes it?
A translation maps A(5, 6) to A′(7, 11). Which rule describes it?

items.q: Reflect A(−1, 5) over the line y = −x. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the line y = −x: (x, y) → (−y, −x). A′ = (−5, 1).

items.q: Reflect A(5, −7) over the x-axis. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y). A′ = (5, 7).

items.q: Reflect A(6, −2) over the line y = −3. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A is 1 unit above y = −3. Go the same distance to the other side: y = −4. The x-coordinate stays. (6, −4).

items.q: Reflect A(4, −7) over the x-axis. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y). A′ = (4, 7).

items.q: Reflect A(−3, −8) over the line y = 4. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A is 12 units below y = 4. Go the same distance to the other side: y = 16. The x-coordinate stays. (−3, 16).

items.q: Reflect A(3, −1) over the line y = −x. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the line y = −x: (x, y) → (−y, −x). A′ = (1, −3).

items.q: Reflect A(4, 7) over the x-axis. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y). A′ = (4, −7).

items.q: Reflect A(−1, −2) over the line y = −x. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the line y = −x: (x, y) → (−y, −x). A′ = (2, 1).

items.q: Reflect A(−1, 8) over the x-axis. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y). A′ = (−1, −8).

items.q: Reflect A(−2, 6) over the x-axis. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y). A′ = (−2, −6).

items.q: The point (−2, 2) is reflected in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a vertical line changes the x-coordinate only: the point is as far on the other side. Image: (2, 2).

items.q: The point (−1, −4) is reflected in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a vertical line changes the x-coordinate only: the point is as far on the other side. Image: (1, −4).

items.q: The point (5, −3) is reflected in the line y = x. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in y = x swaps the coordinates. Image: (−3, 5).

items.q: The point (−5, −4) is reflected in the line x = −2. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a vertical line changes the x-coordinate only: the point is as far on the other side. Image: (1, −4).

items.q: The point (1, −1) is reflected in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a horizontal line changes the y-coordinate only. Image: (1, 1).

items.q: The point (1, −2) is reflected in the line y = −1. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a horizontal line changes the y-coordinate only. Image: (1, 0).

items.q: The point (−5, 4) is reflected in the line y = −2. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a horizontal line changes the y-coordinate only. Image: (−5, −8).

items.q: The point (2, 4) is reflected in the line y = x. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in y = x swaps the coordinates. Image: (4, 2).

items.q: The point (−4, 4) is reflected in the line x = −1. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a vertical line changes the x-coordinate only: the point is as far on the other side. Image: (2, 4).

items.q: The point (3, 4) is reflected in the line y = x. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in y = x swaps the coordinates. Image: (4, 3).

items.q: A rotation about the origin maps A(8, 7) to A′(−7, 8). Which rotation is it?
items.e: Test the rules: (x, y) → (−y, x) gives (−7, 8). 90° anticlockwise.

items.q: Rotate A(−2, −7) 270° anticlockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Rotation 270° anticlockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). A′ = (−7, 2).

items.q: Rotate A(4, −3) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Rotation 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). A′ = (−3, −4). (90° clockwise is the same as 270° anticlockwise.)

items.q: A rotation about the origin maps A(−8, 3) to A′(3, 8). Which rotation is it?
items.e: Test the rules: (x, y) → (y, −x) gives (3, 8). 90° clockwise.

items.q: Rotate A(2, −1) 90° anticlockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Rotation 90° anticlockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). A′ = (1, 2).

items.q: Rotate A(8, −4) 90° anticlockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Rotation 90° anticlockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). A′ = (4, 8).

items.q: Rotate A(7, 6) 90° anticlockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Rotation 90° anticlockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). A′ = (−6, 7).

items.q: A rotation about the origin maps A(−7, −8) to A′(−8, 7). Which rotation is it?
items.e: Test the rules: (x, y) → (y, −x) gives (−8, 7). 90° clockwise.

items.q: Rotate A(−3, −6) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Rotation 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). A′ = (−6, 3). (90° clockwise is the same as 270° anticlockwise.)

items.q: Rotate A(3, 5) 270° anticlockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Rotation 270° anticlockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). A′ = (5, −3).

items.q: The point (−3, 3) is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (−3, 3) from the centre becomes (−3, −3). Image: (−3, −3).

items.q: The point (−4, 0) is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the point (−1, 2). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (−3, −2) from the centre becomes (2, −3). Image: (1, −1).

items.q: The point (3, 1) is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the point (1, 1). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (2, 0) from the centre becomes (0, 2). Image: (1, 3).

items.q: The point (2, −4) is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (2, −4) from the centre becomes (−4, −2). Image: (−4, −2).

items.q: The point (5, 3) is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the point (2, 0). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (3, 3) from the centre becomes (−3, 3). Image: (−1, 3).

items.q: The point (1, 4) is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the point (2, 0). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (−1, 4) from the centre becomes (−4, −1). Image: (−2, −1).

items.q: The point (−4, −4) is rotated 90° clockwise about the point (−1, 2). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (−3, −6) from the centre becomes (−6, 3). Image: (−7, 5).

items.q: The point (−1, −2) is rotated 180° about the point (1, 1). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (−2, −3) from the centre becomes (2, 3). Image: (3, 4).

items.q: The point (3, −2) is rotated 90° clockwise about the point (1, 1). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (2, −3) from the centre becomes (−3, −2). Image: (−2, −1).

items.q: The point (5, 5) is rotated 180° about the point (−1, 2). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (6, 3) from the centre becomes (−6, −3). Image: (−7, −1).

items.q: The point (0, −4) is enlarged by scale factor 0.5 with centre the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: From the origin, multiply both coordinates by 0.5: (0, −2).

items.q: A rectangle 4 cm by 2 cm is enlarged by scale factor 4. What are the new side lengths?
items.e: Multiply every length by 4: 16 cm by 8 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: A rectangle 9 cm by 3 cm is enlarged by scale factor 2.5. What are the new side lengths?
items.e: Multiply every length by 2.5: 22.5 cm by 7.5 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: A side of length 4 cm becomes 10 cm after an enlargement. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Scale factor = new length ÷ old length = 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5.

items.q: The point (−4, 4) is enlarged by scale factor 2 with centre the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: From the origin, multiply both coordinates by 2: (−8, 8).

items.q: The point (2, 1) is enlarged by scale factor 2 with centre the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: From the origin, multiply both coordinates by 2: (4, 2).

items.q: A rectangle 4 cm by 7 cm is enlarged by scale factor 1.5. What are the new side lengths?
c: 2 23 cm by 4 23 cm
items.e: Multiply every length by 1.5: 6 cm by 10.5 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: A rectangle 8 cm by 6 cm is enlarged by scale factor 0.5. What are the new side lengths?
items.e: Multiply every length by 0.5: 4 cm by 3 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: The point (−2, −1) is enlarged by scale factor 2 with centre the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: From the origin, multiply both coordinates by 2: (−4, −2).

items.q: The point (−8, 6) is enlarged by scale factor 0.5 with centre the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: From the origin, multiply both coordinates by 0.5: (−4, 3).

items.q: The point (−4, 8) is enlarged by scale factor 0.5 with centre the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: From the origin, multiply both coordinates by 0.5: (−2, 4).

items.q: A rectangle 6 cm by 2 cm is enlarged by scale factor 3. What are the new side lengths?
c: 2 cm by 23 cm
items.e: Multiply every length by 3: 18 cm by 6 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: A side of length 8 cm becomes 4 cm after an enlargement. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Scale factor = new length ÷ old length = 4 ÷ 8 = 0.5.

items.q: A rectangle 7 cm by 6 cm is enlarged by scale factor 2. What are the new side lengths?
items.e: Multiply every length by 2: 14 cm by 12 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: A rectangle 2 cm by 3 cm is enlarged by scale factor 0.5. What are the new side lengths?
items.e: Multiply every length by 0.5: 1 cm by 1.5 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: A rectangle 5 cm by 8 cm is enlarged by scale factor 4. What are the new side lengths?
items.e: Multiply every length by 4: 20 cm by 32 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: The point (4, −4) is enlarged by scale factor 3 with centre the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: From the origin, multiply both coordinates by 3: (12, −12).

items.q: A side of length 12 cm becomes 3 cm after an enlargement. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Scale factor = new length ÷ old length = 3 ÷ 12 = 0.25.

items.q: The point (−4, 3) is enlarged by scale factor 2 with centre the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: From the origin, multiply both coordinates by 2: (−8, 6).

items.q: The point (6, −8) is enlarged by scale factor 0.5 with centre the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: From the origin, multiply both coordinates by 0.5: (3, −4).

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin
A rotation of 180° about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(1, 2) goes to A′(−2, 1). (x, y) → (−y, x). A rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin.

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin
A rotation of 180° about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(1, 2) goes to A′(1, −2). x stays and y changes sign. A reflection over the x-axis.

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin
A rotation of 180° about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(1, 2) goes to A′(−1, 2). y stays and x changes sign. A reflection over the y-axis.

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin
A rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin
A rotation of 180° about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(2, 1) goes to A′(−2, −1). Both coordinates change sign. A rotation of 180° about the origin.

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin
A rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(2, 2) goes to A′(2, −2). x stays and y changes sign. A reflection over the x-axis.

items.q: Start with A(6, −2): reflect it over the y-axis, then translate it by (x, y) → (x − 1, y + 5). Where does A end up?
items.e: Do the steps in order. After the first step: (−6, −2). After the second step: (−7, 3). The order matters: the other order gives (−5, 3).

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin
A rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(2, 2) goes to A′(−2, 2). y stays and x changes sign. A reflection over the y-axis.

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 180° about the origin
A rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin
A rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(2, 2) goes to A′(−2, 2). (x, y) → (−y, x). A rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin.

items.q: Start with A(−2, 1): translate it by (x, y) → (x − 3, y + 3), then rotate it 180° about the origin. Where does A end up?
items.e: Do the steps in order. After the first step: (−5, 4). After the second step: (5, −4). The order matters: the other order gives (−1, 2).

items.q: Start with A(2, 4): translate it by (x, y) → (x + 1, y − 2), then rotate it 180° about the origin. Where does A end up?
items.e: Do the steps in order. After the first step: (3, 2). After the second step: (−3, −2). The order matters: the other order gives (−1, −6).

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(4, 1) goes to A′(1, 4). The coordinates swap. A reflection over the line y = x.

items.q: Start with A(2, 4): translate it by (x, y) → (x − 3, y + 4), then reflect it over the y-axis. Where does A end up?
items.e: Do the steps in order. After the first step: (−1, 8). After the second step: (1, 8). The order matters: the other order gives (−5, 8).

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 180° about the origin
A rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(2, 1) goes to A′(−3, −5). Every point moves the same way and the triangle keeps its orientation. A translation by (x, y) → (x − 5, y − 6).

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin
A rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin
A rotation of 180° about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(3, 1) goes to A′(1, 3). The coordinates swap. A reflection over the line y = x.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
items.e: A regular polygon with 6 sides has 6 lines of symmetry. 6.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
items.e: A regular polygon with 4 sides has 4 lines of symmetry. 4.

items.q: What is the smallest angle of rotation that maps a regular 12-gon onto itself?
items.e: Rotating by one vertex: 360° ÷ 12 = 30°.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular nonagon have?
items.e: A regular polygon with 9 sides has 9 lines of symmetry. 9.

items.q: What is the smallest angle of rotation that maps a regular pentagon onto itself?
items.e: Rotating by one vertex: 360° ÷ 5 = 72°.

items.q: What is the smallest angle of rotation that maps a regular decagon onto itself?
items.e: Rotating by one vertex: 360° ÷ 10 = 36°.
